caveats.orthology: Reciprocal best hit is one-to-one, so B. rapa's mesohexaploid paralogues are collapsed to a single representative; subfunctionalised copies are invisible to this map.
caveats.preservative: DRS/RL is a large factor in this dataset and is handled as a block, never pooled.
caveats.timing: Harvest times differ between the two experiments, so a shared response could still be missed by sampling at different points of the same kinetic.
caveats.tissue: B. rapa leaf vs OSD-658 whole seedlings; a tissue difference of this size is not separable from a species difference here.

verdicts.aim1: The Arabidopsis-trained decoder does not fire on B. rapa at 40 cGy simulated GCR (index 0.307 at best, threshold 1.96). The decoder is a validated instrument -- it detects 7 of 8 labelled irradiations in Arabidopsis at AUC 0.960 -- so this is a real negative for the projected signature. What it cannot separate is a species difference from the low reliability of this particular dataset.
verdicts.aim2: UNINTERPRETABLE. The B. rapa-native signature fails its positive control: it detects 0 of 12 labelled irradiations, scoring worst of all on a 100 Gy gamma exposure (-3.075). A signature that cannot see 100 Gy tells us nothing by failing to see spaceflight, so its null across the flight corpus is reported as a failed instrument, not as evidence about spaceflight.
verdicts.aim3: NO POWER at gene level. The OSD-658 40 cGy contrast does not reproduce itself (0.0062), so the attenuation cap on any cross-species correlation is 0.0222. The observed value is what that cap predicts regardless of the underlying biology. This says nothing about whether the DNA-damage response is conserved; it says these two datasets cannot be compared gene by gene.
verdicts.what_would_fix_it: Set-level scoring survives noise that per-gene correlation does not, which is why aim 1 is readable and aim 3 is not. A cross-species test at gene level needs contrasts that reproduce themselves: more biological replication per dose arm, or matched harvest timing, before the comparison is worth repeating.
